finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in /dl lets any remote client read arbitrary files the service process can read. filepath.Join lexically cleans '..' segments, so the path escapes /srv/files, and there is no containment check, authentication, or method restriction.
finding.source: files.go:12 r.URL.Query().Get("f") - unauthenticated HTTP query parameter on :8082 (files.go:34 binds all interfaces)
finding.sink: files.go:13 os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)); contents returned via w.Write at files.go:18

trace.note: filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd; Join is lexical cleaning, not containment
sink: os.ReadFile reads the cleaned path
disclosure: w.Write returns file contents to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: filepath.Join is not a containment control. No prefix or Rel containment check, no authentication on /dl (files.go:32), no method, rate-limit, WAF, or symlink check in the code. Absolute f values are contained under root, but .. traversal escapes. Deployment proxy/ingress not visible in repo; reachability established from code (:8082 binds all interfaces); no Shodan or masscan lookup run. Triage Check 13 answered affirmatively on all five questions, so CRITICAL retained; actual ceiling depends on the service account's read permissions. Repro (not run): curl "http://<host>:8082/dl?f=../../../../etc/passwd"
finding.repro: GET /dl?f=../../../../etc/passwd on port 8082 returns HTTP 200 with /etc/passwd contents when vulnerable; a safe build returns 404 for paths outside /srv/files. Not run against any live system.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12-13 takes the raw `f` query value and passes it to filepath.Join(root, name), which only lexically cleans and does not contain the result. There is no prefix or filepath.Rel check, and the error path at files.go:14-16 only returns 404 on read failure. /dl is registered at files.go:32 with no auth, no method check, and no middleware. The only validation in the file is filepath.Base at files.go:22, which applies to the separate /avatar handler and not to /dl.
verdict.reason: At files.go:13, filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, so os.ReadFile reads outside root and files.go:18 returns the bytes to the caller. The route at files.go:32 is unauthenticated and the server listens on all interfaces at files.go:34, so an anonymous remote client can reach it. The real impact depends on the service account's read permissions and on network exposure, which the repo does not show.

finding.claim: Single unauthenticated request for a non-terminating special file (e.g. /dev/zero via traversal) makes os.ReadFile read without EOF and grow memory until the process is OOM-killed. No size limit, regular-file check, or server timeouts exist, so this is a service-wide DoS at negligible cost.
finding.sink: files.go:13 os.ReadFile loads the full stream into memory; files.go:18 w.Write would send it

trace.note: sink: os.ReadFile on a character device that never returns EOF; unbounded allocation
w.Write would transmit the unbounded buffer if it returned

finding.guards_checked: filepath.Join containment: not a control (same root cause as INJ-1). No io.LimitReader or http.MaxBytesReader, no Stat/IsRegular check, no http.Server ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout (files.go:34 uses zero-value server). Triage Check 9: single bounded request with service-wide impact, retained at HIGH. Not reproduced: the behaviour is inferred from Go os.ReadFile semantics and was not run.
finding.repro: GET /dl?f=../../../../dev/zero: vulnerable build never returns and server memory climbs until OOM. Do not run against a live system.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. files.go:12 reads the attacker-controlled `f` with no auth check. files.go:13 uses filepath.Join(root, name), which cleans the path but does not contain it, so `../../../../dev/zero` resolves to /dev/zero. There is no size cap, no Stat/regular-file check, and the handler is registered with no authentication. files.go:34 uses http.ListenAndServe with the zero-value server, so there are no read or write timeouts.
verdict.reason: The attacker is anonymous, since /dl at files.go:32 has no authentication. The traversal at files.go:13 reaches /dev/zero, and os.ReadFile at files.go:13 reads it until EOF, which never comes, so memory grows without bound. Nothing between files.go:12 and files.go:13 blocks this. The memory growth is inferred from Go's os.ReadFile semantics and was not run.
